name: The cow way (drove way) north of Millhaven
region: Millhaven, north-northeast of the top of the east lane

sensoryProfile.sight: A hollow way worn down by carts and cattle 'for longer than the village had had a name', banks higher than a head in places, hazel and thorn meeting overhead, still near night under the hazel at first light; yellow clay floor scored from bank to bank by long parallel grooves 'as if something had dragged a harrow up it with the tines set close', bare-foot and boot prints pocked between them; two old gateposts where it narrows with no gate in a hundred years; bracken on the open hill beyond, the cut a dark seam going over a shoulder.
sensoryProfile.sound: Not described beyond the clicking staff.
sensoryProfile.touch: Clay glazed hard on the groove bottoms where weight had gone over and not let up; rain-rounded edges.
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: A cattle track used by the dead; the place where the girl's account and the ground meet.

establishedFacts.fact: It starts at an open five-barred oak gate at the top of the east lane (the gate swung back against the bank, a loop of rope dropped over the post, 'the way a drover holds a gate for cattle he means to bring through').

It runs north and a little east up out of the fold and over a shoulder of the hill, away from the road down from the Pass, which lies two fields and a hedge west of it and bends away west while the cut goes east of north, the two diverging with distance. The holly wood where the Ch2 ambush happened lies on the Pass road, 'halfway up'.

It heads toward the ward-stones and the long empty miles of ring between one post and the next, where only a warden going round once a fortnight with a lens patrols. (Sylvanas's reasoning, not a stone she has felt.)
Spring grazing: drovers bring the beasts up to the hill grazing in spring and down again about the time of year of the story (autumn).

Cyndia's count with hazel switches, with the mage reading heavy versus light: at least sixty heavy marks, four and five abreast, 'closer than men would'; bunched at the old gateposts; no mark in the cut points downhill; a gap in the bank leads to a farm track and every one went past it; no leader's print found.
The grooves have constant depth with the toe down and weight on it throughout, a forearm's width apart, not the come-and-go of a tired drag.

eventsHere.event: At first light Sylvanas, Cyndia and the mage read the cut and confirm the girl's account; Sylvanas names it a direct border warning.
